_source: Adapted from Valenta et al., 'AMIA Board White Paper: AMIA 2017 core competencies for applied health informatics education at the master's degree level', JAMIA 25(12):1657-1668, 2018.
_note: Each domain has a short label (used as the zero-shot class name) and a longer description used as the hypothesis for NLI-based zero-shot classification (e.g. 'This work is about ...').

domains.label: Health Sciences
domains.description: Clinical foundations, anatomy, physiology, disease processes, pharmacology, and the structure of healthcare delivery; biomedical knowledge needed to understand patient care contexts.

domains.label: Health Information Science and Technology
domains.description: Electronic health records, clinical information systems, interoperability standards such as HL7 FHIR, health information exchange, terminology standards like SNOMED and ICD, and implementation of health IT in care delivery.

domains.label: Social and Behavioral Aspects of Health
domains.description: Patient behavior, social determinants of health, health disparities, cultural competence, user-centered design of health systems, organizational change in healthcare, and human factors in clinical workflows.

domains.label: Information Science and Technology
domains.description: Core computing concepts including databases, software engineering, networks, cybersecurity, cloud platforms, web and mobile development, and information architecture independent of clinical domain.

domains.label: Data Analytics, Decision-Making, and Discovery
domains.description: Statistical analysis, machine learning, data mining, predictive modeling, natural language processing, knowledge discovery, data visualization, and decision support derived from health and biomedical data.

domains.label: Leadership, Professionalism, Project Management, Ethics, and Strategic Thinking
domains.description: Project management, leadership and team management, ethics and privacy regulations such as HIPAA, professionalism, change management, communication, and strategic planning for informatics initiatives.

domains.label: Translational Bioinformatics
domains.description: Genomics, proteomics, precision medicine, integration of molecular and clinical data, and informatics support for translating bench research into bedside applications.

domains.label: Clinical Informatics
domains.description: Clinical decision support, computerized provider order entry, clinical documentation, workflow analysis in clinical settings, quality improvement using informatics, and physician-facing health IT applications.

domains.label: Public Health Informatics
domains.description: Population-level health surveillance, disease registries, public health reporting, environmental and community health data, outbreak detection, and informatics systems supporting public health agencies.

domains.label: Consumer Health Informatics
domains.description: Patient portals, personal health records, mobile health and wellness apps, wearable devices, telehealth, patient education materials, and informatics tools designed for use by patients and caregivers rather than clinicians.
